description: Seeded defects, correct look-alikes and contested constructs of the hard sci-review fixture repository built by build.py. Lines are 1-based and refer to the feature branch. Each entry is located by anchor, a substring that occurs on exactly one line of the file; build.py verifies anchors and lines before every build. score.py matches a finding to an entry when the files are equal and the entry line lies within three lines of the finding range. Reproduction checks resolve relative to this manifest's directory.

defects.description: surface_humidities passes the air pressure in Pa (Forcing.pressure) together with vapour pressures in hPa (units.saturation_vapour_pressure) to specific_humidity, which requires both in the same unit; both humidities, and hence the evaporation and latent heat flux, are 100 times too small. The unit conventions are stated in units.py and forcing.py on main.
defects.wrong_output: q_air = 1.43e-4 kg/kg instead of 1.44e-2 kg/kg

defects.description: The module convention makes every flux positive into the water and sums them for the net flux, but latent_heat_flux returns +L * E, positive when the lake evaporates; evaporation should cool the lake, so the latent term has the wrong sign in the net budget.
defects.wrong_output: +2.76 W/m2 (with the humidity defect; +280 W/m2 once it is fixed) instead of a negative flux

defects.description: Longitudes are east positive (module and units.py docstrings), so local solar time is UTC + longitude / 15 h; the code subtracts the correction, mirroring the sun's path about Greenwich. Sites at longitude 0 are unaffected.
defects.wrong_output: cos(zenith) -0.596 at 06:00 UTC (local noon) and 0.993 at 18:00 UTC (local midnight)

defects.description: Phytoplankton mortality is documented as quadratic and enters detritus as m * P**2, but phyto_loss removes m * P from phytoplankton; the four rates no longer sum to zero, so total nitrogen is not conserved, contrary to the module docstring.
defects.wrong_output: the derivatives sum to 0.3 mmol N m-3 per day instead of 0

defects.description: The sun is above the horizon for hour angles in [-w0, w0], so the day lasts 2 * w0 / 15 hours; the code returns w0 / 15, half the day length.
defects.wrong_output: 6.00 h at the equinox instead of 12 h (7.71 h instead of 15.4 h at the solstice)

defects.anchor: return math.log((surface_light + half_saturation) / (surface_light + half_saturation * math.exp(-kh))) / kh
defects.description: The depth average of I/(I+K) with I = I0 exp(-k z) is ln((I0 + K) / (I0 exp(-kH) + K)) / (kH); the code attaches the exponential to K instead of I0. For a shallow layer it tends to K/(I0+K), the complement of the correct limit I0/(I0+K).
defects.wrong_output: 0.0575 instead of 0.523 (fine quadrature)

defects.description: max_stable_step uses the mean layer thickness, but the explicit scheme is limited by the thinnest layer (dt <= h_min^2 / (2 kappa), as its own docstring derives per layer). On the documented surface-refined grids the reported step, also used to validate explicit_step, is far above the limit; uniform grids are unaffected.
defects.trigger: thicknesses [0.1]*10 + [1.0]*10, diffusivity 1e-4, alternating 20/4 C, 50 steps of max_stable_step()
defects.wrong_output: step 1513 s instead of 50 s; temperatures reach +-1.5e89 C, violating the maximum principle

defects.anchor: likelihood = math.prod(norm * math.exp(-0.5 * (r / sigma) ** 2) for r in residuals)
defects.description: The log-likelihood is computed as the log of a product of densities, which underflows to zero for the documented multi-year hourly series; math.log(0.0) then raises. Summing log-densities is required.
defects.wrong_output: ValueError: math domain error instead of -12715.9

defects.description: euler_run accumulates t += step_days in floating point and loops while t < duration; 24 * (1/24) sums to slightly less than 1, so a one-day run takes 25 steps and ends at 1.0417 days, past the documented end.
defects.wrong_output: 25 steps ending at t = 1.0417 days instead of 24 steps ending at 1

defects.description: The docstring declares reliability weights (only ratios matter), whose unbiased denominator is V1 - V2/V1; the code uses the frequency-weight denominator V1 - 1, so the estimate depends on the scale of the weights and divides by zero when they sum to one.
defects.wrong_output: 0.292, 0.073, 0.0615 instead of 0.073 for every scale

defects.description: mean_confidence_interval pairs Student's t with the population standard deviation (divisor n) instead of the sample standard deviation (n - 1); for the documented three to ten replicates the interval is 6 to 18 % too narrow.
defects.wrong_output: half-width 1.756 instead of 1.963

defects.description: chronological_split fills gaps by linear interpolation over the whole record before cutting it, so a gap that straddles the cut is filled in the training part from the first test value: test data leak into the training targets (and interpolated values are scored as test observations).
defects.trigger: chronological_split([10, 10.5, 11, 11.5, None, None, None, None, 14, 14.5], 0.5), then with 20 in place of 14
defects.wrong_output: last training value 12.0 becomes 13.2 when only a test value changes

defects.description: run_implicit assembles the diagonals once and reuses them every step, but solve_tridiagonal (tridiag.py on main) overwrites diag in place during elimination; from the second step on the solver works with the eliminated diagonal, so multi-step runs (spin_up) are wrong and do not conserve heat.
defects.wrong_output: heat content 2.888e8 J/m2 becomes 6.449e8 J/m2 with no flux

defects.anchor: y, error = bogacki_shampine_step(f, t, y_old, h)
defects.description: integrate assigns the trial solution to y before the error test; when the step is rejected, the retry starts from the rejected state at the old time instead of from y_old, so every rejection corrupts the solution.
defects.wrong_output: y(0.2) = 1.18e-3 after 4 rejections instead of exp(-10) = 4.54e-5

defects.description: Profile temperatures are in kelvin (types.ts on main), but sensorDensities passes them to densityOf, whose formula expects degrees Celsius; schmidtStability and heatmap.ts convert with toCelsius, this function does not.
defects.trigger: sensorDensities of a profile at 277.13 K
defects.wrong_output: 759.65 kg/m^3 instead of 1000.0

defects.anchor: out.push({ time: sample.time, depth: depthFromPressure(sample.pressure, met[index].pressure) });
defects.description: Barometric pressure in MetSample is in hPa (types.ts on main) while depthFromPressure requires Pa; subtracting hPa from the absolute transducer pressure leaves the atmosphere in the hydrostatic term, adding about 10.2 m to every depth.
defects.wrong_output: 15.23 m instead of 5.00 m

defects.description: Schmidt stability needs the depth of the centre of volume, integral z A dz / integral A dz, as its docstring states; the code uses the mid-depth, which equals it only for vertical-walled basins. A uniformly mixed lake that narrows with depth then has non-zero stability.
defects.trigger: uniform 285.15 K profile, hypsography depths 0..20 m with areas 1e6 .. 1e3 m^2
defects.wrong_output: -3.67e5 J/m^2 instead of 0

defects.description: The second-order one-sided stencil (-3, 4, -1)/(2h) holds only for equal spacing; the module documents uneven sensor depths (0.5, 1, 2 m ...), for which the stencil weights must be derived from h1 and h2. With unequal spacing the result is not even first-order accurate, contrary to the claimed exactness for quadratics.
defects.wrong_output: 0.625 K/m instead of 0

defects.description: The standard error of the OLS slope is sqrt(SSE / (n - 2) / Sxx); the code divides by Sxx outside the square root, which is dimensionally wrong (units of slope per unit time) and wrong by a factor sqrt(Sxx).
defects.wrong_output: 0.0796 instead of 0.2517; scaling t by 10 divides it by 100 instead of 10

defects.description: rollingStd differences running sums of x and x^2 over the whole series; for the documented absolute pressures (about 1.5e5 Pa, months of minute data) the prefix sums of squares reach 1e15 and more, so the window variance is lost to cancellation and clamped to zero.
defects.wrong_output: last-window std 0 Pa instead of 0.0357 Pa

defects.anchor: const slope = (n * sty - st * sy) / (n * stt - st * st);
defects.description: leastSquares uses the raw normal-equation sums with times in ms since the epoch (about 1.8e12); n * sum(t^2) - (sum t)^2 cancels catastrophically whenever the time span is short relative to the epoch offset, which the daily long-term panels hide but bursts and short windows expose.
defects.trigger: 600 samples 100 ms apart from 2026-06-01, y = 12 + 1e-6 (t - t0)
defects.wrong_output: slope 7.67e-7 instead of 1e-6

defects.description: The result documents a two-sided p-value, but 1 - Phi(|Z|) is the one-sided tail; the two-sided value is 2 (1 - Phi(|Z|)). Trends are declared significant at half the stated level.
defects.wrong_output: p = 0.00064 instead of 0.00128

defects.description: correlation drops NaN from each series separately, so after a gap in one series the remaining values are paired with values from other times; pairwise deletion must remove the pair.
defects.trigger: a = [1, 4, 2, NaN, 5, 3, 6, 2, 7], b = 2a with NaN at index 1
defects.wrong_output: 0.923 instead of 1

defects.description: The search finds the first abscissa greater than x; for x equal to the last abscissa, documented as admissible, none exists, right = n and the formula reads past the array, returning NaN (heat maps and resampling at the deepest sensor).
defects.wrong_output: NaN instead of 280

defects.description: dailyMeans counts days from the first sample instead of from 00:00 UTC, so a series that does not start at midnight is grouped into 24-hour windows straddling calendar days and stamped with the wrong time, contrary to the documented UTC calendar days.
defects.trigger: 24 hourly samples from 2026-06-01 12:00 UTC, 1 on June 1 and 3 on June 2
defects.wrong_output: one day stamped 2026-06-01T12:00Z with mean 2 instead of two days with means 1 and 3

defects.description: densityOf memoises on temperature alone although the density depends on salinity; after a lookup for fresh water, saline water at the same temperature returns the fresh-water density (and vice versa), across profiles and lakes for the life of the page.
defects.wrong_output: 999.728 kg/m^3 for 8 g/kg instead of 1006.058

lookalikes.description: Declination uses sin(2 pi (n - 81) / 365) while the docstring cites Cooper's sin(2 pi (284 + n) / 365); since 284 + n = (n - 81) + 365 the two are identical.
L = 2.501e6 - 2361 t is the standard linear fit with t in degrees Celsius, the module's temperature unit; it is not a kelvin/Celsius mix-up.
Solving K/2 = K / (1 + (K/N0 - 1) exp(-r t)) gives exp(-r t) = 1 / (K/N0 - 1), i.e. t = ln(K/N0 - 1) / r; the expression is correct under the documented precondition N0 < K/2.

The surface and bottom rows carry a single exchange term (1 + r rather than 1 + 2r); this is the finite-volume no-flux condition, as the docstring explains, and equals the general expression because the missing coefficient is zero.

lookalikes.anchor_end: return T_975[max(k for k in T_975 if k <= df)]
lookalikes.description: The t table falls back to the normal quantile above 120 degrees of freedom and rounds df down otherwise; the docstring bounds the error (at most 1 %, no worse than the table's own rounding), so this is a documented approximation.
n (1 - rho) / (1 + rho) is the standard large-n effective sample size of the mean of an AR(1) series; the formula is correct.
1 W m^-2 over 86400 s is 0.0864 MJ m^-2 day^-1; the factor is exact.
Exact equality on depths is correct: they are nominal configuration values copied unchanged, never computed, as the docstring states.

lookalikes.anchor: for (const t of ties.values()) tieTerm += t * (t - 1) * (2 * t + 5);
lookalikes.description: Var(S) = [n(n-1)(2n+5) - sum t(t-1)(2t+5)] / 18 is the standard tie-corrected Mann-Kendall variance; the constants are correct.
The unusual constants are those of the published simplified Chen-Millero fresh-water density, in degrees Celsius as documented; the formula is correct.

contested.description: The bulk formulae use fixed transfer coefficients of 1.3e-3, an open-water neutral value referenced to 10 m wind, with the measured wind speed whatever its height. Forcing.wind_height documents 10 m shore stations and 2 m buoys; at 2 m the wind is roughly 20-25 % lower in neutral conditions, so fluxes from buoy forcing are biased low, while shore-station forcing is consistent. Stability corrections are also omitted.
contested.expected_deciding_assumption: Whether the forcing used with these coefficients is measured at (or adjusted to) 10 m in near-neutral conditions; shore-station forcing is, but the documented 2 m buoy forcing is not, and nothing adjusts it.

contested.description: The percentile bootstrap resamples daily mean residuals independently. If daily residuals are serially uncorrelated the interval is valid; lake-temperature residuals are often autocorrelated over days (the module itself warns that series are autocorrelated), in which case an iid bootstrap understates the width and a block bootstrap is needed.
contested.expected_deciding_assumption: Whether the daily mean residuals over the test period are serially independent; nothing in the code tests or corrects for their autocorrelation.

contested.description: Depth from hydrostatic pressure uses a constant 1000 kg/m^3. For cold fresh water the error is below 0.3 %, comparable to transducer accuracy; for warm water (996 kg/m^3 at 27 C) or the network's saline lakes (up to about 1008 kg/m^3 at 10 g/kg, see types.ts and density.ts) the depth is off by 0.4-0.8 %, i.e. several centimetres at 10 m.
contested.expected_deciding_assumption: Whether the transducer stations are in fresh, cool water and centimetre-level depth accuracy is not required; for saline or warm lakes a density from temperature and salinity is needed.
